web_title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape—Stop Breached in Stage 4 Liquidation
question: Why did TSM break its $348.00 structural stop on 2.38x volume, how do our two technical feeds diverge, and what exact base-and-reclaim proof is needed before re-entering?

epigraph.quote: The first rule of surviving a Stage 4 break is never to argue with a violated stop. Great companies can still lose 30% to 50% when institutional supply overwhelms the tape.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein, Stage Analysis

web_blocks.title: Weekly & Daily Breakdown: Stop Breached & Two-Feed Stage Split (CAP_REJECTED)

web_blocks.html: On November 20, 2026, TSM suffered a decisive technical breakdown despite record October revenue (+59.7% YoY) [22, 35]. The stock plunged -9.48% in a single day from $352.09 to close at $318.71 ($319.14 on TradingView), finishing -20.07% for the week and -34.62% off its $487.47 52-week high [28, 35]. Most critically, closing at $318.71 shattered our prior $348.00 structural stop by $29.29 (-8.42%). Heavy institutional liquidation drove the move, with 37.17 million shares trading—2.38x the 20-day average (2.36x the 30-day average of 15.78M) [28, 35].

We must also disclose a mechanical divergence between our two market-data feeds as of November 20, 2026. The deterministic `facts_US_2026-11-20.json` ledger tags TSM as Stage 1 (Basing) solely because $318.71 sits right on its $318.48 63-day low (`base_pivot_atr: 0.01`, `vol_dryup_ratio_63d: 0.50`) [35]. In sharp contrast, our `snapshots_US_2026-11-20.json` evaluation classifies TSM as STAGE_4 / AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN (`CAP_REJECTED`) [28]. That `STAGE_4` call reflects reality: price trades -24.5% below a falling 50-day SMA ($422.15), -21.0% below its 200-day SMA ($403.56), and -23.6% below its 30-week SMA ($417.72) on 9 distribution days in 25 sessions [28, 35].
Reviewing weekly, daily, and 4-hour price action side by side shows uniform institutional distribution across every timeframe [28, 35].

web_blocks.takeaway: Every timeframe from 4H to Weekly confirms Stage 4 liquidation below all major moving averages on 2.38x distribution volume, invalidating the prior $348.00 stop and enforcing CAP_REJECTED.

web_blocks.html: Our multi-timeframe `options_US_batch4.json` chart readout underscores why catching this falling knife is dangerous [28]. On the 4-hour chart, RSI dropped to an oversold 22.47 while price crashed to $319.14—nearly $50 below the 4H EMA20 ($368.26) and $79 below the 4H SMA50 ($398.06), leaving `intraday_4h_turn: false` [28]. On the daily tape, ATR-14 widened from $17.10 to $19.06 (5.98% of share price), and Bollinger Band width expanded to 38.61% [28, 35]. Meanwhile, 63-day relative strength stands at -12.64% (-17.06% over 28 days) [35].

Live options telemetry from `options_snapshot.py` (`options_US_batch4.json`) flags TSM as NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID for automated trade execution today. Option bid-ask spreads exceed our 14% slippage ceiling or lack qualifying open interest across the screened contracts, and the macOS Chrome Robinhood probe is unavailable in this Linux environment. Even if spreads tighten intraday on NYSE exchanges, buying bullish calls or debit spreads into a Stage 4 waterfall (`CAP_REJECTED`, `REJECTED`) violates our fundamental-technical safety interlock. Zero options exposure is authorized.

web_blocks.title: Why Oversold RSI (28.26 Daily / 22.47 4H) Is Not a Buy Signal
paragraphs: Deeply oversold RSI readings often tempt value buyers into calling a bottom after a -20% week. In Stan Weinstein's framework, oversold readings in Stage 4 frequently precede sharp dead-cat bounces into falling averages—like the 4H EMA20 ($368.26) or 20D SMA ($391.78)—followed by another leg lower. Real bottoms require weeks of sideways absorption where volume dries up and price stops making lower lows below $318.48.

web_blocks.html: The broader tape offers zero tailwinds. As of November 20, 2026, the S&P 500 shifted into a formal Downtrend, with 10 distribution days in 25 sessions and 38.8% of stocks above their 50-day SMA (46.9% above 200-DMA) [35]. Only 1 of 11 sectors holds its 20-day SMA, and just 17.0% of semiconductor peers hold above their 50-day EMA [28, 35]. Crucially, the automated `snapshots_US_2026-11-20.json` screen still prints legacy moving-average bands (`$391.08–$428.49` support buy zone and `$408.20` stop anchored near the `$422.16` 50-day SMA) [28]. Because TSM collapsed to `$318.71`, `$391.08–$428.49` and `$408.20` are broken historical levels now acting as heavy overhead trapped supply above `$318.71`—NOT nearest support. Every shelf from Pivot S2 (`$343.89`) and our breached `$348.00` stop up through `$428.49` represents trapped supply, leaving the `$318.48` 63-day low and `$266.82` 52-week low as the real downside levels [28, 35].

web_blocks.title: What Technical Proof Is Required to Exit REJECTED?

web_blocks.html: TSMC remains on our fundamental compounder radar (`COMPOUNDER_PASS`), so we define clear, objective conditions to re-underwrite it later [28, 35]. Step 1 requires price to carve a durable Stage 1 floor—either holding the $266.82–$290.00 52-week low zone or stabilizing above $318.48 for at least 4 to 8 weeks while 20-day and 50-day averages flatten [35]. Step 2 requires volume dry-up on down days followed by institutional accumulation (>1.2x average volume on strong closes). Step 3 requires a decisive Stage 2 breakout back above the 200-day SMA ($403.56) and 30-week SMA ($417.72) on >1.2x volume as market breadth recovers [28, 35].

Until those three steps occur, the tape overrides valuation. TradingView's overall technical score sits at -0.65 (Strong Sell), with a -0.93 moving-average score [28]. Disciplined capital steps aside at $318.71, honors the breached $348.00 stop, and waits for sellers to finish.

book_paragraphs: Chapter 7 showed that TSMC's valuation has compressed to 13.81x forward earnings. Chapter 8 delivers the cold reality of the tape: on November 20, 2026, TSM suffered a severe Stage 4 breakdown that violated our $348.00 structural stop and forced a full exit.

In a single session, TSM fell 9.48% from $352.09 to $318.71 ($319.14 on TradingView), completing a -20.07% weekly drop on 37.17 million shares—2.38 times its 20-day average volume. The stock now sits 34.62% below its $487.47 52-week high and has broken cleanly below every intermediate support shelf.

Let us be transparent about a technical feed split. Our deterministic market-facts ledger mechanically labels TSM Stage 1 Basing because $318.71 sits right on its $318.48 63-day low. Our TradingView snapshot flags STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED). Anyone looking at the moving averages sees why Stage 4 wins: TSM trades 24.5% below its falling 50-day SMA ($422.15), 21.0% below its 200-day SMA ($403.56), and 23.6% below its 30-week SMA ($417.72).

Worse, the macro backdrop deteriorated from a Correction into an outright US Downtrend, logging ten distribution days in twenty-five sessions with only 38.8% of stocks above their 50-day moving average. In that tape, oversold oscillators do not protect buyers.

book_callouts.title: Why Breaking $348.00 Forces Immediate Action
book_callouts.text: Our prior monograph set $348.00 as the non-negotiable guardrail below the $351.19 swing low. Closing at $318.71 on 2.38x volume breached that stop by nearly $30. Hoping for a rebound after a broken stop is how small losses become permanent drawdowns.

book_subsections.title: Reading the 1W, 1D, and 4H Tape Together After the Crash
paragraphs: Walking across all three timeframes shows uniform technical damage. On the weekly chart, TSM sits 23.60% below its $417.72 30-week SMA and 19.62% below its $397.04 10-week EMA, with weekly RSI down at 33.48. On the daily chart, TSM sits 5.43 ATR units below its falling 50-day SMA ($422.15), while ATR-14 expanded to $19.06—nearly 6% daily volatility.

Drop down to the 4-hour chart from options_US_batch4.json and there is still no bottoming turn. TSM closed nearly $50 below its $368.26 4H 20-EMA and $79 below its $398.06 4H 50-SMA, with 4H RSI crushed to 22.47 and intraday_4h_turn false. Every rally back toward $343.89 (Pivot S2) or $368.26 now meets trapped supply.

book_subsections.title: Why Options Are Sidelined: Illiquid Spreads and Broken Trend
paragraphs: Our options engine (`options_US_batch4.json`) flags TSM as NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID in this session because screened option bid-ask spreads exceed 14% or lack qualifying open interest, while the macOS Chrome Robinhood probe is unavailable in this Linux workspace.

Even more importantly, our discipline strictly forbids buying bullish calls or debit spreads on a stock in Stage 4 below its broken stop. Capital belongs in cash, not fighting heavy institutional distribution.

book_subsections.title: Overhead Supply Psychology and Sector Breadth Breakdown
paragraphs: Think about the overhead supply created between August and November 2026. Millions of shares changed hands between $375 and $487.47. Notice that our automated snapshot screen still displays legacy moving-average bands ($391.08–$428.49 and $408.20) anchored to the 50-day SMA ($422.16). At $318.71, those broken historical levels are NOT nearest support—they are heavy overhead supply alongside Pivot S2 ($343.89) and our breached $348.00 stop.

Sector breadth confirms that this is not an isolated shakeout. Only 17.0% of semiconductor peers hold above their 50-day EMA, and just one of eleven S&P 500 sectors holds its 20-day moving average. When institutions liquidate an entire leadership group at 2.38x normal volume, rallies into falling moving averages get sold until supply dries up.

book_subsections.title: The Road Back: What a Real Stage 1 Base Looks Like
paragraphs: Stepping aside today does not mean ignoring TSMC forever. A compounder growing sales 40%+ with $93.64 billion in net cash will eventually attract institutional accumulation again. First, the waterfall must stop—watching whether buyers defend the $266.82–$290.00 zone or stabilize above $318.48 over four to eight weeks.

Second, we need to see volume dry up on pullbacks and expand above 1.2x average on strong up-closes, flattening the 50-day SMA. Third, TSM must reclaim its 200-day ($403.56) and 30-week ($417.72) moving averages alongside improving S&P 500 breadth before new capital returns.
